question: Which operations can change the local library's membership or metadata, how are those mutations serialized, and how is filesystem/index disagreement repaired?

requiredFacts.description: The mutation surface includes addPdf, refreshMetadata, remove, restore, reconciliation, and repair.
Mutations are serialized across processes by the per-library SQLite mutex before reading and changing folded index/filesystem state.
Adds and metadata refreshes append add events, removal appends rm, restoration appends restore, and events identify records by ID plus version.
Remove and restore reject a destination collision, rename the PDF between papers and trash before appending the matching event, compact, and return the new state.
answerEvidenceAlternatives: exists in both papers and trash

requiredFacts.description: Reconciliation adds or restores discovered live files, adds then removes unindexed trash files, removes indexed-live records missing from disk, validates matching files, and compacts when it changed the log.
Repair holds the mutex, rejects unsupported index versions, tolerates corruption, backs up the index, discovers papers and trash, reuses or reconstructs records, and writes a compact rebuilt index.

answerIncludesAny: the remove event is appended before moving the file
the restore event is appended before moving the file
repair redownloads missing PDFs from arXiv
